She had brought her trusty Zora armor with her, but she realized that it was not very practical for this type of environment.
One of the first things Princess Ruto did was to go on a tour of the castle, and she was fascinated by all of the intricate details and ancient artifacts. However, as she walked through the castle, she couldn't help but feel the urge to relieve herself. She had been in Hyrule for only a few hours, and already her bladder was starting to ache.
Princess Ruto tried to hold it in, but it was no use. She quickly found a bathroom and let out a relieved sigh as she finally emptied her bladder. She was grateful for the modern plumbing and sanitation of Hyrule, but she couldn't help but feel a bit self-conscious about her accident.
Despite her initial embarrassment, Princess Ruto was warmly welcomed by the people of Hyrule, who were fascinated by her Zora heritage and curious about her home in the water. She spent her time in Hyrule exploring the beautiful landscapes and getting to know the kind and friendly people. She even helped Princess Zelda on a quest to defeat a powerful enemy and save the kingdom.
In the end, Princess Ruto returned to her home in the water, but she left behind a lasting impression on the people of Hyrule. They would always remember the kind and adventurous Zora who had visited their kingdom, and the lessons she had taught them about the importance of embracing differences and being open to new experiences.
